course.programmeTitle: Bachelor of Engineering in Data Science and Engineering
course.title: Business Intelligence and Analytics
course.description: This course provides both theoretical understanding and practical experience in business intelligence and analytics. Students will explore data warehousing concepts, ETL processes, multidimensional modeling, and visualization techniques. Through Power BI labs, they will develop interactive dashboards, perform data-driven analysis, and deliver insights that support business strategy and operations.

clos.description: Explain the fundamental concepts, architectures, and roles of Business Intelligence and Analytics in organizational decision-making.
Design and develop data models and dashboards in Power BI to support data-driven business insights.
clos.teachingMethodsRaw: Lab Sessions, Guided Exercises, Live Demo

clos.description: Analyze and interpret business data to derive actionable insights and communicate findings effectively through visual reports
clos.teachingMethodsRaw: Case Study, Lab Work, Group Discussion

clos.description: Demonstrate teamwork, ethical responsibility, and professional conduct in delivering BI solutions for real-world business problems.
clos.teachingMethodsRaw: Project-Based Learning, Group Work, Peer Collaboration

topics.title: Topic 1: Introduction to Business Intelligence & Analytics
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Define Business Intelligence (BI) and Analytics; explain their importance in organizational decision-making. LLO2: xxx

topics.title: Topic 2: BI Architecture and Data Ecosystem
topics.llosRaw: Describe BI system components (data sources, ETL, warehouse); explain how data flows across systems

topics.title: Topic 3: Data Warehousing Concepts
topics.llosRaw: Identify fact and dimension tables; design a simple star schema for analytical databases.

topics.title: Topic 4: ETL and Data Preparation
topics.llosRaw: Perform data extraction, transformation, and loading (ETL) using Power Query in Power BI.

topics.title: Topic 5: Data Modelling in Power BI
topics.llosRaw: Build relationships between tables and manage data integrity in Power BI.

topics.title: Topic 6: DAX Fundamentals
topics.llosRaw: Create calculated columns and measures using basic DAX functions (SUM, AVERAGE, IF).

topics.title: Topic 7: Visualization Design Principles
topics.llosRaw: Apply design principles (layout, chart types, color use) to create clear and effective visuals.

topics.title: Topic 8: Advanced DAX and Data Analytics
topics.llosRaw: Implement advanced DAX functions (Time Intelligence, dynamic KPIs) to enhance dashboard capability.

topics.title: Topic 9: Dashboard Design & User Interaction
topics.llosRaw: Develop interactive dashboards using filters, slicers, and bookmarks in Power BI.

topics.title: Topic 10: Storytelling with Data
topics.llosRaw: Interpret analytical results and communicate insights through narrative visualizations.

topics.title: Topic 11: Business Case Analytics
topics.llosRaw: Apply BI techniques to a real-world business case (e.g., sales, HR, or logistics data).

topics.title: Topic 12: Team Project Development
topics.llosRaw: Collaborate in groups to plan, design, and implement a BI dashboard project.

topics.title: Topic 13: Ethics, Privacy, and Governance in BI
topics.llosRaw: Demonstrate ethical data handling and deliver professional project presentations.

topics.title: Topic 14: Final Project Presentation & Peer Evaluation
topics.llosRaw: Present final BI dashboards professionally and evaluate peers’ work constructively.

studentResponsibilitiesRaw: Read the learning materials beforehand which means to be ready for the next session. Be completely engaged in class, active, take notes, and ask questions in class. Students are required to participate in various activities in and out of the classroom, such as group work, and individual homework for assignments and reports assigned by the subject teacher. Submit the assigned tasks such as homework, assignments, or research proposal on time.
coursePolicyRaw: Attendance & Preparation Students are expected to attend all classes (online/on-site). Assigned readings and preparation outlines must be completed before class if any. Active participation in group discussions and post-chapter evaluations is required. Academic Integrity All assignments, quizzes, and exams must be done individually. Academic misconduct includes: - Presenting others’ work as one’s own. - Engaging in plagiarism or cheating. Homework & Assignments Preparation outlines must be submitted on time; late submissions incur penalties. Peer discussion is encouraged, but midterm and final exams must be independent. Examinations Midterm and final exams are closed-book. Penalties Violations of academic integrity may result in a failing grade and referral to the Office of Student Affairs. Students uncertain about potential violations should consult the instructor in advance.
